💊 What is PharmaFast? PharmaFast is an Android application built to help pharmacy owners manage their medicine inventory and sales efficiently. The goal was to design a simple, lightweight app tailored for fast-paced pharmacy environments.
🚀 Features 📦 Real-time inventory management 🧾 Sales tracking & billing 🔍 Medicine search with autocomplete 🔔 Low-stock notifications 📊 Dashboard for quick insights 📱 Built using Java and Android Jetpack 🎥 Demo Video 📺 [Watch on YouTube]
🛠️ Tech Stack Language: Java Architecture: MVVM Database: Firebase UI: Material Design Tools: Android Studio 🔗 GitHub Repository 👉 View PharmaFast on GitHub
👤 Role & Contribution This was a solo project. I designed, developed, and tested the app from scratch. It reflects my focus on clean architecture, user-first design, and mobile performance.
Thanks for checking it out! 😊
summary: A mobile app for pharmacy inventory and sales management, designed for speed and simplicity.
title: PharmaFast – Android App

🎮 What is VideoGame DB? VideoGame DB is a responsive Angular web application that lets users search, filter, and explore video games using live data from the RAWG Video Games Database API. It was designed with performance, user experience, and responsiveness in mind.
🌟 Features 🔎 Real-time search with autocomplete 🎮 Browse games by genre, platform, rating, and release year 🧭 Detailed pages for each game with rich metadata 📱 Fully responsive and mobile-friendly layout 🔄 Clean, reactive UI with Angular and RxJS 🚀 Live Demo 👉 Try the Live App
Hosted on Firebase
💻 GitHub Repository 👉 View Source Code on GitHub
🛠 Tech Stack Framework: Angular (v16+) Language: TypeScript Styles: SCSS, Angular Material API: RAWG Video Games API Hosting: Firebase 👩‍💻 My Role This is a solo project that showcases my skills in:
Component-based architecture Consuming REST APIs State and route management Responsive UI design with Angular Material 🚧 Next Steps Add user authentication (Google Sign-In) Save favorite games Add infinite scroll and improved loading states Thanks for checking it out!
summary: A video game browsing web app built with Angular, consuming RAWG API.
title: VideoGame DB – Angular App

content:
🎬 What is the Client Movie App? Client Movie App is a full-stack web application built to explore modern DevOps practices alongside full-stack development. The app allows users to browse, filter, and interact with a collection of movies — all while integrating an end-to-end CI/CD workflow using Docker, GitHub Actions, and deployment automation.
🌟 Features 🖥️ Frontend built with React 🌐 Backend API powered by Spring Boot 🐳 Dockerized frontend and backend apps 🔁 GitHub Actions for automated build, test, and deployment 📦 Deployed as multi-container setup via Docker Compose 🔗 GitHub Repository 👉 View on GitHub
🛠 Tech Stack Frontend: React, JavaScript, Axios, CSS Backend: Spring Boot, Java, REST APIs Database: PostgreSQL DevOps Tools: Docker (multi-container) GitHub Actions Docker Compose CI/CD pipeline Environment variables and secrets management 👩‍💻 My Role This was a solo project with the goal of combining:
Full-stack web development Hands-on DevOps practices
summary: A full-stack movie app with a CI/CD DevOps pipeline, built using React and Spring Boot.
title: Client Movie App – DevOps Project

content:
📘 What is Reddit Clone? Reddit Clone is a full-stack Blazor web application that replicates the core functionalities of Reddit — allowing users to register, create posts, vote, and comment. The project showcases the power of Blazor Server, real-time data updates, and full CRUD operations in a reactive C# web environment.
🌟 Features 🧑 User authentication and registration 📝 Post creation with rich text editor 👍 Voting system (upvote/downvote) 💬 Nested commenting 🗂️ Subreddits (categories) 🔍 Sort and filter posts by popularity or date 🚀 Live Demo (Host this on Azure, no longer running)
🛠 Tech Stack Frontend & Backend: Blazor Server (.NET 7) Database: Entity Framework Core + SQL Server Identity: ASP.NET Core Identity for user auth UI: Bootstrap 5 Other: SignalR (optional for real-time), LINQ, Dependency Injection 💻 GitHub Repository 👉 View on GitHub
👩‍💻 My Role This is a solo project created to deepen my understanding of:
Blazor’s component-based architecture State management with cascading parameters and dependency injection Building modular, reusable Razor components Integrating secure user identity and authorization in .NET 📈 Future Improvements Add post search and tagging Implement notifications with SignalR Dark mode toggle Mobile responsiveness improvements Thanks for reading! Feel free to star the repo or fork it if you’re building your own forum clone.
summary: A Reddit-style forum clone built using Blazor, Entity Framework, and a modern .NET stack.
title: Reddit Clone – Blazor Web App

Hey, I’m Aitana 👋 Welcome to my corner of the internet! I’m a developer, tinkerer, and proud code nerd who decided to stop keeping my projects hidden in GitHub repos and start sharing them with the world.
This site is my digital playground—a place where I showcase the things I build, write about tech (and occasionally break things just to fix them again 😉), and reflect on my journey in software development.
💡 Why This Site? I’ve always loved creating things. Whether it’s designing sleek front-ends, building out APIs, or debugging something at 2am that “should have worked”—I find joy in the process.
So why this site?
To showcase my projects: Android apps, Blazor sites, DevOps pipelines—you name it. To write and share what I learn along the way. To document my growth and maybe inspire someone else. 👩‍💻 A Little About My Journey I studied Software Development and dove head-first into the world of tech. Along the way, I’ve worked on a wide range of projects—from building pharmacy delivery apps and movie platforms to developing Reddit-style forums using Blazor, Angular, and more.
Here’s a taste of what I’ve played with:
Frontend: Angular, React, Blazor Backend: .NET, Node.js DevOps: CI/CD, GitHub Actions Other stuff I love: clean code, open source, and pixel-perfect UI ✨ 🚀 What to Expect Here Project deep dives – real talk on what went right, what broke, and how I fixed it Tech tutorials – bite-sized guides on tools I use or learn Reflections – thoughts on the tech industry, my career, and maybe even the occasional rant 😅 🌍 Outside of Code… When I’m not glued to my keyboard, you might find me:
Sketching out designs Playing games and breaking them down for fun Drinking way too much coffee ☕ Dreaming about my next side project Thanks for stopping by! Explore, connect, and feel free to reach out if you want to collaborate, share ideas, or just geek out over tech.
– Aitana
